What I read is main. Revision c3c36da, the one that ran, is not in main's history, so I have not seen it. I am relying on the investigation's account of its diff (metrics -> http-metrics).

On main, `deploy/values-production.yaml` sets `metrics.portName: http-metrics`. On main, the ServiceMonitor in `deploy/scrape.yaml` selects its endpoint with `port: metrics`. The header comment in `deploy/scrape.yaml` says the scrape picks the target by the port's name, and that "a name that matches no port is not an error to the operator, it is a target list with nothing in it". So once the port was renamed, the scrape found no targets and samples stopped. The shop kept serving, as the logs show. The rename was a deliberate, platform-wide convention, so rolling it back is not the fix. The fault is that the scrape config lagged behind it and nothing checked the two against each other.

The change:
- `deploy/scrape.yaml`: `port: metrics` becomes `port: http-metrics`, so it matches the port name main's values file gives. Nothing else in the file changes.
- New test `tests/io_shop/test_deploy_config.py`: it reads `metrics.portName` from `deploy/values-production.yaml` and every `port:` entry under the ServiceMonitor's `endpoints` in `deploy/scrape.yaml`, and asserts they are the same name. It parses both files with plain line scanning, so it doesn't need a YAML library. Against main's `deploy/scrape.yaml` before this change, it should fail (`metrics` != `http-metrics`). With the change it should pass. A future rename that touches only one of the two files would fail the test before merge. No test runner was available, so none of this has been run.

Caveat: this fixes the config in the repository. Whoever deploys still has to apply the updated ServiceMonitor (or redeploy the chart from a branch that includes it). If c3c36da's branch has its own copy of `deploy/scrape.yaml`, it needs the same one-line change.

# How the platform's Prometheus collects the shop's metrics.
#
# The ServiceMonitor the platform applies with the shop's chart, kept in the
# repository beside how the shop is deployed, so that how it is collected
# changes in the same pull request as what it is collected from.
#
# It selects the shop's Service by label, then the endpoint to scrape on that
# Service by the port's *name* - never its number - so a port can move without
# anything here being touched.
#
# The name here has to be the one `metrics.portName` in values-production.yaml
# gives the port. Nothing checks that the two agree: a name that matches no port
# is not an error to the operator, it is a target list with nothing in it.
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: ServiceMonitor
metadata:
  name: io-shop
  labels:
    release: prometheus
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: io-shop
  endpoints:
    - port: http-metrics
      path: /metrics
      interval: 15s
